title: HB1189 (2018 Regular): Public Safety – Handgun Permits – Protective Order and Peace Order

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2018RS/bills/hb/hb1189f.pdf)
provenance.note: first_reader: bill as filed; no vote recorded. The first quote joins separate sub-items; the first alternative is existing law.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-306(a)(6)(ii)): 1. has good and substantial reason to wear, carry, or transport a handgun, such as a finding that the permit is necessary as a reasonable precaution against apprehended danger; OR 2. IS: A. A PERSON ELIGIBLE FOR RELIEF UNDER A CURRENT CIVIL PROTECTIVE ORDER ENTERED UNDER § 4–504.1, § 4–505, OR § 4–506 OF THE FAMILY LAW ARTICLE; B. UNDER THE PROTECTION OF A CURRENT ORDER FOR PROTECTION, AS DEFINED IN § 4–508.1 OF THE FAMILY LAW ARTICLE, THAT HAS BEEN ISSUED BY A COURT OF ANOTHER STATE OR A NATIVE AMERICAN TRIBE; OR C. A PETITIONER UNDER A CURRENT PEACE ORDER ENTERED UNDER TITLE 3, SUBTITLE 15 OF THE COURTS ARTICLE.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-306(e)): THE SECRETARY SHALL ISSUE A PERMIT FOR AN APPLICANT SPECIFIED IN SUBSECTION (A)(6)(II)2 OF THIS SECTION WITHIN 10 CALENDAR DAYS AFTER RECEIPT OF THE APPLICATION.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-309(e)): A PERMIT ISSUED TO AN APPLICANT SPECIFIED IN § 5–306(A)(6)(II)2 OF THIS SUBTITLE EXPIRES 5 YEARS AFTER ISSUANCE.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-312(b)(2)): WITHIN 10 CALENDAR DAYS AFTER RECEIVING A REQUEST FROM AN APPLICANT SPECIFIED IN § 5–306(A)(6)(II)2 OF THIS SUBTITLE TO REVIEW A DECISION OF THE SECRETARY, THE BOARD SHALL: (I) REVIEW THE RECORD DEVELOPED BY THE SECRETARY; OR (II) CONDUCT A HEARING.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-312(e)): IN THE CASE OF A REQUEST FROM AN APPLICANT SPECIFIED IN § 5–306(A)(6)(II)2 OF THIS SUBTITLE TO REVIEW A DECISION OF THE SECRETARY, THE BOARD SHALL SUSTAIN, REVERSE, OR MODIFY THE DECISION OF THE SECRETARY WITHIN 5 CALENDAR DAYS AFTER REVIEWING THE RECORD OR CONDUCTING A HEARING.
